unit.title: From Disjoint-Set Theory to a Reliable Connectivity Component
unit.scope: Design, implement, test, and explain one Java union-find component and one bounded connectivity client.
learning_objectives: State representation invariants and use them in a correctness argument.
Implement weighted union with path compression behind a precise Java API.
Build deterministic boundary, invalid-input, integration, and model-based tests.
Apply monotone connectivity to a small event-stream problem without duplicating the core algorithm.
Record reproducible build evidence and discuss operational limits such as mutability and concurrency.
out_of_scope: Claiming completion of Algorithms I, Algorithms II, or the catalog's approximately 60-hour course
Reconstructing or submitting any of the ten described official projects
Using unverified lecture, textbook, starter-code, solution, or autograder content
Supporting edge deletion, persistence, distributed execution, or a thread-safe API

unit_completion_requires: All listed learner deliverables exist and are attributable to the learner attempt.
A worker-harness-controlled validator independently compiles and runs the implementation and tests.
The validator checks behavior, algorithmic constraints, documentation, and comprehension against the examiner-only rubric.
Validation evidence is durable and explicitly labeled; learner prose alone is not accepted as proof.
completion_policy.on_unit_success: Mark only unit_kickoff_union_find_engineering_v1 complete; retain the course as incomplete and awaiting evidence-backed expansion.
completion_policy.course_completion_rule: This kickoff can never establish whole-course completion. Completion requires a separately defined graph of verified later units and independent validation of every required unit.
completion_policy.failure_rule: Preserve failed-attempt artifacts and evidence; a retry does not erase prior results.
